# Buffer `faff config dump` output before printing

## WHY
`faff config dump` writes each resolved key with a separate `process.stdout.write`. On a large `.faffrc.yaml` that is dozens of tiny syscalls; one buffered write is cleaner and avoids interleaving when stderr is also active.

## WHAT
Collect the rendered dump lines into an array and emit them with a single `console.log(lines.join('\n'))`; the output bytes and exit code are unchanged.

## HOW
**Chosen:** assemble the lines in the existing render loop and flush once at the end. No change to the rendering of any individual line, so the output is byte-identical.

**Punt:** whether the buffer should default to in-memory (simplest, almost certainly right for any real `.faffrc`) or stream through a tempfile for a hypothetical pathologically-large config — flagging for a human, not blocking; in-memory is the obvious default and a tempfile path can be added later if a real config ever needs it.

## DONE
- [ ] `faff config dump` produces byte-identical output to the pre-change per-line version
- [ ] exactly one stdout write occurs for the dump body
- [ ] a unit test asserts the single-write behaviour and unchanged bytes

The core work is fully specified; one non-blocking open question remains on the buffer-backing choice, where the in-memory default is almost certainly right.
